author: nvddr
body:
## Summary

Implements `xr_media_hub.ipc` — the shared-memory + ZMQ IPC layer that decouples the LiveKit connector from agent code. Two dependencies only: `pyzmq` and `msgpack`.

- **ConnectorEndpoint**: producer — writes CPU frames into a shm ring buffer, signals hub via ZMQ PUSH. Creates and owns its own ring buffer; registers with hub on startup.
- **HubEndpoint**: server — dispatches `on_frame`, `on_audio`, `on_data`, `on_participant` callbacks; resolves connector topology via registry; enforces participant isolation (no cross-participant routing).
- **ShmRingBuffer**: 64-byte slot headers, zero-copy memoryview reads.
- Multi-track: `FrameSignal` and `AudioChunk` carry `(participant_id, track_id)`; ZMQ topics namespaced as `audio.<pid>.<track>` for prefix-filter subscriptions.
- Bidirectional: `send_return_audio/data()` lets agents push back to XR clients.
- Dynamic join/leave via `notify_participant_joined/left()` — no static participant lists.

## Test plan
- [ ] ConnectorEndpoint can push frames and audio without deadlocking
- [ ] HubEndpoint dispatches all callbacks correctly
- [ ] Return path reaches the correct participant only
- [ ] Multi-connector topology is transparent to consumer callbacks

author: amatabsc
body:
The implementation of VPinVdMicroInst incorrectly defined the source register array with insufficient capacity. When used in vslideup.vx with masking enabled, the micro-op registers three source operands (undisturbed vd, rs1, and v0), but the array was only sized for two.
This caused a buffer overflow that overwrote destRegIdxArr[0] with the v0 register identifier, effectively redirecting writes to the mask register instead of the intended destination vector register.
As a result, instructions like vslideup.vx could corrupt v0, diverging from the expected behavior where the mask register remains unchanged.
Expanding srcRegIdxArr to hold three entries fixes the overflow and ensures the destination register is preserved correctly across all micro-ops.

## Summary
- Root cause: Default-constraint validation skipped every pair containing type parameters, so defaults or constraints that were bare references to another type parameter never reached assignability and missed TS2344 diagnostics.
- Fixed conformance target: `TypeScript/tests/cases/compiler/genericDefaultsErrors.ts`
- Fix: validate default/constraint assignability when either side is a bare reference to another type parameter, while preserving skips for self-references and derived generic defaults.

## Unit Tests
- `test_type_parameter_default_constraints_validate_type_parameter_references`
- `test_type_parameter_default_constraints_skip_self_and_derived_type_parameter_references`

## Verification
- `scripts/session/verify-all.sh` passed after final fetch/rebase on `origin/main` `75db6d888a`.
- Summary: formatting, clippy, unit tests, conformance `12099` vs baseline `12089` (`+10`), emit tests `JS +0, DTS +8`, fourslash/LSP `50/50`.

## Diagnostic Proof
The checker now emits TS2344 at the default for bare type-parameter references like:

```ts
declare function f<T, U extends number = T>(): void;
declare function g<T, U extends T = number>(): void;
```

**What is being fixed:** The integration test `DisplayPageInfoItemFieldSetProviderTest.testGetInfoFieldValuesWithConfiguredURLSeparator` is flaky — it occasionally reads the default URL separator (`/e/`) instead of the custom one configured by the test.

**How it is being fixed:** In `FriendlyURLSeparatorConfigurationManagerImpl.updateFriendlyURLSeparatorCompanyConfiguration`, `saveCompanyConfiguration` fires the Config Admin update asynchronously, and the local `PortalCache` is cleared immediately after. A concurrent read landing in the window between the save and the asynchronous event propagation can repopulate the just-cleared cache with the stale value (read through `ConfigurationProvider`'s own cache, which has not been invalidated by the event yet).

After `saveCompanyConfiguration` returns, this change polls `ConfigurationProvider.getCompanyConfiguration` until the stored `friendlyURLSeparatorsJSON` matches what was just written (20 ms interval, 10 s timeout, warn-and-continue on timeout) before clearing the local cache. This directly verifies the invariant we care about — the config store has propagated — without introducing new synchronization primitives.

author: sonicaj
body: This commit adds changes to fix a subtle issue where `missing_required_datasets` failed to detect when the root docker dataset itself was missing. The check constructed its fatal set using `set(docker_ds)`, which iterates the dataset path string character-by-character (e.g. `"tank/.ix-apps"` becomes `{'t','a','n','k','/','.','i','x','-','p','s'}`) rather than producing a single-element set containing the path. As a result, the root dataset was never included in the intersection check and a missing root docker dataset would silently pass validation instead of raising a `CallError` during docker startup. The fix replaces `set(docker_ds)` with `{docker_ds}` so the full dataset name participates in the fatal-set membership check as intended.

body:
Previously the warning page pulled state through three separate injection mechanisms:
  1. `<meta name="dappfence-token">` for the API token
  2. Inline feature-flag "trueValues" object read via getFeatureFlag()
  3. Runtime fetch to /sw-api/active-blocks for block details

Collapse all three into a single `DAPPFENCE_CONFIG` object inlined into the `<script>` block. Page renders synchronously, no token querySelector, no feature-flag shim, no async fetch + error UI. The config statement is emitted via `encodeURIComponent` + a double-quoted string literal. Double quotes are load-bearing: `'` is in encodeURIComponent's unreserved set, so wrapping in single quotes would let an attacker-supplied apostrophe close the literal. A test guards against a formatter or edit flipping the quote style.

Also moves CSS inlining and the build-time feature-flag evaluation to module scope they're static across renders and were being recomputed on every block.

`renderBlocks` now hides the Active Blocks section when the list is empty; previously the section was always shown after fetch- success, so an edge-case empty list would render "Active Blocks (0)".

## Résumé — ce qui a été fait

Derniere polish de la Phase 3 : les nodes du talent tree montrent maintenant la vraie icône de spell WoW au lieu d'un cercle gris. Transforme visuellement le builder + le viewer — on identifie les talents au coup d'œil.

**1 commit atomique** : script + JSONs régénérés + type + rendering indissociables (partial merge = icônes manquantes ou lookups crashés).

## Changements

1. **`scripts/fetch-talent-trees.ts`** : après normalisation des specs, collecte l'ensemble des spell ids uniques (ranks + choices), fetche `/data/wow/media/spell/{id}` par batch de 8, back-fill `iconUrl` sur chaque `NormalisedSpell`. Runtime ~4 min pour 3158 spells uniques.

2. **Les 40 JSONs régénérés** avec `iconUrl` — taille passe de 1.9 MB → 2.5 MB total (+600 KB pour les URLs). **2603/3158 spells (82%) ont une icon** ; le reste sont des placeholders ou talent-node-only spells sans endpoint media — fallback automatique sur le shape plat coloré.

3. **`TalentSpell`** en `@gc/shared/simbot` : nouveau champ optionnel `iconUrl` documenté. Rétrocompatible.

4. **`<TalentTreeView>`** rend chaque node comme SVG `<image>` clippé en cercle (SINGLE/PASSIVE/ACTIVE) ou rounded rect (CHOICE), avec un stroke overlay pour l'état picked (emerald épais) vs défaut (border fin). Unpicked → icon à 55% opacity, picked → 100%. Defs réutilisent 2 clipPaths pour tout le tree (un par shape) — DOM reste léger.

## Points importants à reviewer

- **Icons = URLs Blizzard CDN complètes** (`https://render.worldofwarcraft.com/.../xxx.jpg`) stockées tel quel dans les JSONs. Si Blizzard change le hash CDN (arrive rarement), relancer `pnpm tsx scripts/fetch-talent-trees.ts`. Même fenêtre que le bump simc, cohérent avec la règle documentée dans `CLAUDE.md`.
- **82% coverage** — les 18% sans icon sont soit des placeholders (testing / beta spells), soit des talents purement mécaniques (passifs sans spell visuel). Fallback sur fill plat = acceptable, pas de degraded UX notable.
- **Pas de cache HTTP custom** — on laisse le browser cacher les images via les headers Blizzard (Cache-Control: public). À l'ouverture d'un tree, ~100 icons chargent en parallèle, après quoi tout est instant tant que les URLs ne bougent pas.
- **CORS** — les URLs Blizzard CDN servent `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Le `<image>` SVG marche, pas de préflight bloquant.
- **Picked state** = stroke emerald 2.5px (vs 1.5px), pas de teinte emerald sur l'icon elle-même — préserve la lisibilité du spell. Pattern similaire aux in-game talents (bord doré quand selectionné).
- **`unavailableNodeIds`** (de PR #47 prereqs) **non mergée dans cette branche** — les deux PRs sont parties de main indépendamment. Merge conflict trivial à attendre dans `TalentTreeView.tsx` (les deux ajoutent des props différentes). Si tu merges #47 avant #48, rebase ce diff pour intégrer le `opacity-30` du strict mode sur le stroke + garder `iconOpacity` sur l'image. Je peux rebaser si tu préfères.
- **`<image href>`** plutôt que `xlinkHref` — SVG2 standard, bien supporté par tous les browsers modernes incluant Next.js SSR.

## Points à tester manuellement

- [ ] **Build** : `pnpm --filter web build` passe (testé localement).
- [ ] **Visuel** : ouvrir `/simbot/talent-builder`, Priest Holy → toutes les icônes apparaissent (pas de cercles gris). Switch vers Warrior Fury, DH Havoc, Evoker Aug → même chose.
- [ ] **Fallback** : certains nodes (minoritaires) peuvent encore afficher un cercle/carré gris — c'est le comportement attendu quand le media API n'a pas renvoyé d'icon.
- [ ] **Picked state visible** : cliquer un node → stroke emerald plus épais, icon à 100% opacity. Unpicker → retour à 55% + stroke border.
- [ ] **CHOICE nodes** : carrés arrondis avec icon clippée en rounded square. Click cycle 0 → 1 → unpick comme avant.
- [ ] **Tooltip inchangé** — hover sur un node montre le nom du spell via `<title>` natif.
- [ ] **Page `/simbot/report/:id`** : icons visibles aussi (viewer read-only partage le même composant).
- [ ] **Pas de régression** : import, export, Effacer, stats, switch class/spec, tous OK.

body:
Lock bots to a fixed tick rate, use a per-frame accumulator that can handle a variable timer.

This solves a bunch of timing-related issues I was seeing with long-running sessions (many hours) in a Xash3D-FWGS dedicated server (`v49/0.21 (linux-amd64 build 4037)`).

The bots would behave normally initially, and then as the round progressed, they would eventually start taking longer and longer to "think" or "tick".

In the server console, the debug prints would show `total difference` gradually creeping up with no players in the server (causing the bots to behave "choppy"), and would gradually creep back down when a player joined.

I've been running this on my server for a few hours and haven't seen any of these issues since. I'll leave it run overnight, but I'm pretty sure this fixes it.

EDIT: Confirmed, bots are still working properly after running overnight.

## Bug

Forgot-password SMS delivered the signup template:

> Your HRNG OTP for account registration is 123456. It is valid for 10 minutes. Do not share this OTP with anyone.

Regardless of flow (signup vs reset), \`sendOtpSms\` used a single \`FAST2SMS_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE\` / \`FAST2SMS_TEMPLATE_ID\`. Reset-password users saw the same "account registration" wording.

## Fix

\`sendOtpSms\` now accepts a \`purpose: "SIGNUP" | "RESET_PASSWORD"\` argument and selects the template per-purpose.

New env vars (all optional, fall back to the existing single-template vars):

**DLT route** (\`FAST2SMS_ROUTE=dlt\`):
- \`FAST2SMS_TEMPLATE_ID_SIGNUP\`
- \`FAST2SMS_TEMPLATE_ID_RESET\`

**DLT manual route** (\`FAST2SMS_ROUTE=dlt_manual\`):
- \`FAST2SMS_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_SIGNUP\`
- \`FAST2SMS_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_RESET\`

\`authController.sendOtp\` passes the chosen \`OTPPurpose\` through; \`forgotPassword\` pins \`"RESET_PASSWORD"\`.

## Ops follow-up

Register a second DLT template (\`HRNGPZ\` sender) for password reset, e.g.:

> Your HRNG OTP for resetting your password is {#VAR#}. It is valid for {#VAR#} minutes. Do not share this OTP with anyone.

Once approved, set on server:

\`\`\`
FAST2SMS_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_RESET=Your HRNG OTP for resetting your password is {otp}. It is valid for {minutes} minutes. Do not share this OTP with anyone.
\`\`\`

Until that's set, reset flow continues falling back to the signup template (no regression vs. current behaviour).

## Affected files

- \`api/src/services/sms.ts\`
- \`api/src/controllers/authController.ts\`

- [ ] Signup OTP → still delivers signup template (unchanged)
- [ ] Forgot password OTP without reset env var → falls back to signup template (unchanged, no break)
- [ ] Forgot password OTP with \`FAST2SMS_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_RESET\` set → delivers reset-specific template

### Motivation
- Add a detectors layer to turn raw features into per-epoch detector results containing soft scores, reason codes, hard-fail flags and local metrics to support supervisor decision logic.
- Provide both immediate hard-gate checks and softer anomaly/statistical detectors so downstream fusion can combine deterministic failures with graded risk scores.

### Description
- Added a detector framework with shared base and helper: `detectors/base.py` defines `Detector` and `clamp01` for score clamping. 
- Implemented a hard-fail detector `HardGatesDetector` (`detectors/hard_gates.py`) that checks no-fix timeout, stale-data timeout, impossible jump, frozen-solution, and extreme HDOP and emits `DetectorResult` with `hard_fail`, `reason_codes`, `score`, and `metrics`.
- Implemented soft detectors: `KinematicAnomalyDetector` (`detectors/kinematic_anomaly.py`) using normalized jump/speed/course/climb metrics, `StaleDataDetector` (`detectors/stale_data.py`) using gap/stale/frozen/backwards features, `ModeFlapDetector` (`detectors/mode_flap.py`) measuring validity and fix-type toggles and reacquisition instability (with a type-fix to store fix-type as `str`), and `StatisticalDetector` (`detectors/statistical.py`) with simple EWMA/CUSUM-style scoring over jump, speed mismatch and HDOP.
- Exported detectors from `detectors/__init__.py` and added acceptance-focused tests `tests/test_hard_gates.py` and `tests/test_detector_outputs.py` that assert hard-fail behavior, mode-flap sensitivity, healthy-sequence low scores, and global score clamping to `[0,1]`.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_hard_gates.py tests/test_detector_outputs.py` and both test files passed.
- Ran the full `pytest -q`; the detector tests pass but the full test run shows 2 failing tests in the existing NMEA parser/adapter tests that are unrelated to the new detectors (those pre-existing failures were not caused by the detector additions).

author: ixchio
body:
## What's wrong

**1. Zombie Deno workers**

`kill()` fires SIGTERM and schedules SIGKILL 5s later. But `cleanup()` runs in `execute()`'s finally block and nulls out `this.process` before the timer fires — so SIGKILL never reaches the process. Each leaked worker can hold up to 8GB.

**2. `callAxios` can silently return `undefined`**

The function is typed as `Promise<CallAxiosResult>` but there's no return/throw after the `do...while`. `noImplicitReturns` isn't on in tsconfig so TS doesn't catch it. If anyone touches the retry logic and accidentally creates a new exit path, callers like `notifyWebhook` will blow up with `Cannot destructure property 'response' of undefined`.

## What I changed

- **deno-worker.ts**: Capture process ref in a local var before cleanup can null it. SIGKILL fires unconditionally (since `proc.killed` is already `true` after any `.kill()` call — Node.js quirk), wrapped in try-catch for the case where the process exited on its own.
- **http.ts**: Added `throw new ApiCallError(...)` after the loop. Defensive, but it makes the type contract honest.

## Tests

- 9 new tests covering the race condition, retry behavior, and return type soundness
- all existing tests still pass

## 概要

kernel `Mailbox::run()` の未使用 `_throughput_deadline` 引数を実際に enforce し、Pekko `Mailbox.scala:261-278` が規定する「throughput 本数 × deadline」合成条件の yield 契約を完全に再現する。gap-analysis MB-M1 (medium) 対応。

関連: `openspec/changes/pekko-mailbox-throughput-deadline/`

## Pekko 契約との行単位対応

Pekko `Mailbox.scala:275`:
```scala
(left > 1) && (!dispatcher.isThroughputDeadlineTimeDefined || (System.nanoTime - deadlineNs) < 0)
```

fraktor-rs 実装 (post-decrement while loop + post-invoke break):
```rust
while left > 0 && self.should_process_message() {
  // L268-269: dequeue
  // L271: actor.invoke(next)
  // L274: processAllSystemMessages() — deadline break より先に評価 (Pekko 順序厳守)
  left -= 1;
  // L275: deadline break
  if let Some(da) = deadline_at
      && self.clock.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c() >= da)
  {
    break;
  }
}
```

- `left > 0` (post-decrement) ≡ Pekko `left > 1` (pre-decrement 再帰)
- `c() >= da` ≡ Pekko `nanoTime >= deadlineNs` (deadline 到達で break)
- deadline 計算は `run()` 先頭で 1 回: `deadline_at = clock.zip(throughput_deadline).map(|(c, d)| c() + d)`

## Summary

Adds on-demand video frame pixel delivery to `ProcessorEndpoint` and enforces NVIDIA hardware codec availability at startup.

**Video frame delivery**: processors receive `FrameSignal` metadata at full rate via `on_frame()` — no pixel copy per frame. Pixels only copied on explicit `await ep.request_frame(signal)`. ## Summary

- Add application-level `withNetworkRetry` wrapping every `generateContent` call in `ask`, `code`, and `ask_agentic` (incl. stale-cache retry paths). 3 attempts with exponential backoff 1s → 3s → 9s.
- Root cause: `p-retry` 4.6.2 (pinned by `@google/genai` 1.50.x) routes any `TypeError` outside its browser-era whitelist (`"Failed to fetch"`, `"Network request failed"`, …) to `operation.stop()` — Node 18+ undici emits `TypeError: fetch failed` for every pre-response failure, so SDK-side retry cannot help even with `httpOptions.retryOptions` enabled.
- Intentionally do NOT enable `httpOptions.retryOptions` in `createGeminiClient`: briefly tried; the SDK's retry path wraps non-retryable responses via `p-retry` and replaces Gemini's informative error body (`ApiError: {"error":{"code":400,"status":"INVALID_ARGUMENT", …}}`) with a generic `"Non-retryable exception Bad Request sending request"` that strips the `INVALID_ARGUMENT` details callers and the smoke test rely on.

## Scope

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Breaking change

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added (`test/unit/gemini-retry.test.ts`, 14 tests covering `isTransientNetworkError` classification + `withNetworkRetry` behaviour: first-success, retry-on-transient, non-transient propagation, budget exhaustion, `attempts` clamp to `[1,10]`, `onRetry` hook, exponential backoff timing).
- [x] Integration smoke test (`test/integration/real-gemini.smoke.test.ts`) continues to pass with unchanged error-shape expectations — the brief F1 experiment that broke it is reverted.
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (biome: 59 files, no fixes).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `npm run test` — 22 files / 407 tests pass (was 393; +14 new).
- [x] `npm run build` — clean.

## Details

Empirical matrix of `withNetworkRetry` classification and routing is codified in the test file. Key behaviours:

| Input | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `TypeError('fetch failed')` (Node undici) | transient → retry up to `attempts-1` times |
| `err.cause.code ∈ {ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EAI_AGAIN, …}` | transient → retry |
| `Error` with numeric `.status` | non-transient → propagate immediately |
| `AbortError` | non-transient → propagate immediately |
| Plain `Error('validation failed')` | non-transient → propagate immediately |

Backoff formula: `baseMs * 3^(attempt - 1)` → `1s`, `3s`, `9s` with `baseMs: 1000` default.

## Known limitation

Documented in `docs/KNOWN-DEFICITS.md`: once `@google/genai` updates its pinned `p-retry` to 6.x (which uses the `is-network-error` package and recognises Node undici errors natively), the app-layer retry can be narrowed — either to HTTP status codes the SDK still misses, or removed entirely.

## Changeset

- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated with `[1.5.1] — 2026-04-22` section (Fixed + Changed + Developer notes).
- [x] `package.json` / `package-lock.json` bumped `1.5.0` → `1.5.1`.

body:
Follow-up to #288. Addresses two post-merge review findings from Cursor Bugbot.

## Changes

### 1. \`encode_nft_number\` returns \`std::expected\`

Before, the helper returned a bare \`data_chunk\` and produced an empty
vector both for the valid encoding of \`0\` AND on the error path
(e.g. \`INT64_MIN\`, whose two's-complement negation is UB and is
rejected by the underlying \`number::from_int\`). Callers couldn't tell
a successful \`0\` from a silently corrupted input.

New signature:

\`\`\`diff
- data_chunk encode_nft_number(int64_t value);
+ std::expected<data_chunk, std::error_code> encode_nft_number(int64_t value);
\`\`\`

BCHN's \`CScriptNum::serialize\` guards \`INT64_MIN\` the same way (\`validRange\`
check before negation); libauth's \`bigIntToVmNumber\` sidesteps the
problem entirely by taking a \`bigint\`. With \`int64_t\` we propagate the
error up so the caller's \`.value()\` is unambiguous.

Tests: BCHN reference vectors, power-of-two boundaries, realistic
counter sizes, negative round-trips — all updated to use \`.value()\` /
\`->size()\`. Two new cases assert that \`INT64_MIN\` is rejected with an
error and that \`INT64_MAX\` round-trips to an 8-byte encoding.

### 2. \`create_token_transfer\` rejects out-of-range fungible amounts

Previously \`ft_amount\` was only checked against zero. A value above
\`INT64_MAX\` would reach \`make_fungible\` and produce an unsigned
transaction that only failed at broadcast-time token validation. The
genesis builder already had the correct check; this adds the matching
check to transfer.

\`\`\`diff
- if (want_ft && *params.ft_amount == 0) {
-     return std::unexpected(kth::error::token_amount_overflow);
- }
+ if (want_ft) {
+     uint64_t const ft = *params.ft_amount;
+     if (ft == 0 || ft > static_cast<uint64_t>(INT64_MAX)) {
+         return std::unexpected(kth::error::token_amount_overflow);
+     }
+ }
\`\`\`

Two new test cases: reject \`ft_amount == 0\` and reject \`ft_amount > INT64_MAX\`.

## Not addressed (by design)

Cursor Bugbot also flagged that \`script_flags\` has no in-class
initialiser, so \`params p;\` (default-init without braces) reads
indeterminate. This was an explicit design decision in #288 ("no le
pongas default a los flags porque es algo crucial"): callers are
required to initialise the field. \`params{}\` (aggregate value-init)
still gives 0 (Descartes) safely, which is the documented usage.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`cmake --build . --target domain\` succeeds
- [ ] \`./src/domain/kth_domain_test [cashtoken_minting]\` — all tests pass

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes wallet token-building APIs by altering `encode_nft_number`’s return type and tightening fungible-amount validation; callers may need updates and behavior now fails fast on previously-accepted edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Hardens CashTokens minting/transfer validation.** `encode_nft_number` now returns `std::expected<data_chunk, std::error_code>` and propagates VM-number encoding failures (notably rejecting `INT64_MIN`) instead of returning an empty chunk that could be confused with the valid encoding of `0`.
> 
> `create_token_transfer` now rejects fungible transfer amounts outside the VM range (`0` or `> INT64_MAX`) to prevent building transactions that only fail later during network token validation. Tests are updated for the new `expected` API and add coverage for the new edge-case rejections.

Added smoother visual transitions when search results update, so filtering feels less abrupt.
Simplified the Study Set header search behavior to avoid awkward movement when clearing search.
Search input now behaves in a more stable, predictable way during open/clear actions.
2) Study Set API fetch reliability fix
Updated API base URL resolution in StudySet to avoid hardcoded localhost-only behavior in non-local environments.
Improved fetch error handling with a clearer network/server-unreachable message.
This reduces “Failed to fetch” confusion and gives users actionable feedback.
3) Responsive sidebar / hamburger navigation
Kept desktop sidebar behavior for large screens.
Hid fixed sidebar on smaller screens and introduced a hamburger-triggered slide-in drawer.
Added backdrop + close interactions and auto-close on item selection for better mobile/tablet usability.
Fixed a hook-order issue in App.jsx that caused a blank page after responsive navigation changes.
4) Subject card action visibility update
Edit and delete icons on subject blocks are now always visible (not hover-only), improving discoverability and accessibility.
5) Safer delete flow (GitHub-style typed confirmation)
Replaced native window.confirm delete prompt with a custom confirmation modal.
Users must type delete my subject before delete is enabled.
Added smooth open/close modal animation and smoother button interactions for Cancel/Delete.

body:
## Summary

Extracts the agent IPC layer into a standalone package, enforces subprocess venv isolation, reorganizes per-sample config, and expands AGENTS.md into a complete sample authoring guide.

**agent-sdk** (`agent-sdk/`): new `xr-ai-agent` package containing `_types`, `_codec`, `_shm`, `_processor` — moved from `server-runtime`. Agents depend only on `xr-ai-agent` + `xr-ai-launcher` — no LiveKit, FastAPI, uvicorn, numpy, or cryptography. `xr-media-hub` re-exports everything for backwards compatibility.

**Subprocess isolation**: each sample has two sub-projects — orchestrator (depends only on `xr-ai-launcher`) and worker (depends only on `xr-ai-agent` + task libs). `ProjectLauncher` runs any uv project as a managed subprocess via `uv run --project`. `run_stack` is fail-fast: any process exit terminates the whole stack. ZMQ reconnects automatically so `ProcessorEndpoint` tolerates the hub not being ready at startup.

**Config reorganization**: `xr_media_hub.yaml` moved into each sample directory; `HubLauncher` upward-walk finds it immediately. `server-runtime/xr_media_hub.yaml` serves as the documented reference.

**AGENTS.md expansion**: naming conventions, full directory layout, `pyproject.toml` templates, orchestrator boilerplate, annotated worker `__main__.py` template, worker code rules, new-sample checklist.

## Test plan
- [ ] `uv sync` in a sample worker succeeds without pulling in LiveKit/FastAPI
- [ ] `run_stack` starts hub + agent concurrently; killing one terminates both
- [ ] Echo-agent and VLM-agent work correctly after isolation refactor
- [ ] Per-sample `xr_media_hub.yaml` discovered automatically by `HubLauncher`
